Estimate the split-half reliability of a heterogeneous transition network

Source: R/reliability_htna.R
reliability_htna.Rd

reliability_htna() estimates the split-half reliability of one or more htna networks: how far each network would look the same if it had been estimated from a different half of the sessions. The sessions are split at random into two halves many times, a network is estimated from each half, and the two networks are compared: the mean, median and maximum absolute difference of their edge weights and the correlation of their weights. High correlations and small deviations over the splits indicate that the estimated structure does not depend on which sessions happened to be observed.

When several networks are given (for example, built with different methods from the same data), each is assessed with the same splits. reliability_htna() runs Nestimate's network_reliability(), and the networks re-estimated on the splits keep the actor partition. It returns an htna_reliability object.

For the stability of the weights when increasing shares of the sessions are dropped use casedrop_reliability_htna(); for edge-level intervals use bootstrap_htna().

Usage

reliability_htna(..., iter = 1000L, split = 0.5, scale = "none", seed = NULL)

Arguments

...

One or more htna networks from build_htna().

iter

Number of random splits (default 1000).

split

Proportion of the sessions in the first half (default 0.5).

scale

Scaling of the weights before they are compared: "none" (default), "minmax", "standardize" or "proportion".

seed

Random seed (default NULL, no seed is set).

Value

An object of class c("htna_reliability", "net_reliability") with print(), summary() and plot() methods. summary() returns a data frame with one row per network and metric and columns model, metric (mean_dev, median_dev, cor, max_dev), mean and sd.

Conditions

An error of class htna_empty_input when no network is given, and of class htna_bad_input when an input is not an htna network.

See also

casedrop_reliability_htna(), bootstrap_htna(), centrality_stability_htna().

Examples

data(human_ai)
net <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (42 sessions), 'actor_type' (24 sessions)
rel <- reliability_htna(net, iter = 30, seed = 1)
rel
#> Split-Half Reliability (30 iterations, split = 50%)
#>   Mean Abs. Diff.     mean = 0.0123  sd = 0.0010
#>   Median Abs. Diff.   mean = 0.0074  sd = 0.0009
#>   Pearson             mean = 0.9824  sd = 0.0041
#>   Max Abs. Diff.      mean = 0.0980  sd = 0.0289
summary(rel)
#>      model     metric        mean           sd
#> 1 relative   mean_dev 0.012347097 0.0009948951
#> 2 relative median_dev 0.007373837 0.0008943957
#> 3 relative        cor 0.982368095 0.0041061329
#> 4 relative    max_dev 0.097975625 0.0288536573
